questions.question: If 25 people working 15 hours a day can complete 5 units of work in 8 days, how many days would be required by 12 persons to complete 10 units of work, working 20 hours a day?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the **MDH/W relation**: **(M₁ × D₁ × H₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) / W₂**

⇒ (25 × 8 × 15) ÷ 5 = (12 × D × 20) ÷ 10

⇒ 600 = 24 × D

⇒ D = 600 ÷ 24 = 25 days

**∴ The correct answer is 25 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: M₁ = **25 persons**, H₁ = **15 hr/day**, D₁ = **8 days**, W₁ = **5 units**

Case 2: M₂ = **12 persons**, H₂ = **20 hr/day**, W₂ = **10 units**, D₂ = ?

**Formula Used:**

The work done is proportional to the product of persons, days, and hours: (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) / W₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/90bd6df853aacb4933365e51b889eddf623336a73218399627510fb4eb0087a7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (25 × 8 × 15) / 5 = (12 × D₂ × 20) / 10

⇒ 5 × 8 × 15 = 12 × D₂ × 2

⇒ 600 = 24 × D₂

⇒ D₂ = 600 ÷ 24

⇒ D₂ = 25

**∴ The correct answer is 25 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

The Chain Rule Formula

It is defined as M₁D₁H₁E₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂E₂/W₂, where E represents the efficiency of the workers.

Direct and Inverse Proportion

The number of **men** is **inversely proportional** to **days** and **hours**, but **directly proportional** to the **work** completed.

Work & Wages

Wages are generally distributed in the ratio of the **total work done** by each person or group (Efficiency × Time).</p

questions.question: Jaggu can make one wooden chair in 3 days and Rabbu can make the same chair in 4 days. If they work together, in how many days will they make 14 chairs of the same kind?

questions.question: Ravi and Kumar are working on an assignment. Ravi takes 6 hours to type 32 pages on a computer, while Kumar takes 5 hours to type 40 pages. How much time will they take, working together on two different computers to type an assignment of 110 pages?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Ravi's** rate = 32 ÷ 6 = 16/3 pages/hr.

**Kumar's** rate = 40 ÷ 5 = 8 pages/hr.

**Combined rate** = 16/3 + 8 = 40/3 pages/hr.

Time for **110 pages** = 110 ÷ (40/3) = 33/4 = 8.25 hours = 8 hr 15 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hr 15 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Ravi** types 32 pages in 6 hours.

**Kumar** types 40 pages in 5 hours.

Total assignment size = 110 pages.

**Formula Used:**

Work = Rate × Time ⇒ Rate = Work ÷ Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d71d3522f70483627ce209df9e4df1cbefe6583172558576e77d26db960503b1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Typing speed of **Ravi** = 32/6 = 16/3 pages/hr

⇒ Typing speed of **Kumar** = 40/5 = 8 pages/hr

⇒ Combined speed = (16/3 + 8) pages/hr

⇒ Combined speed = (16 + 24) ÷ 3 = 40/3 pages/hr

⇒ Time taken to type **110 pages** = 110 ÷ (40/3)

⇒ Time = (110 × 3) ÷ 40 = 330 ÷ 40 = 33/4 hours

⇒ Time = 8.25 hours

⇒ 8.25 hours = 8 hours + (0.25 × 60) minutes

⇒ Time = 8 hours 15 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hr 15 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Work-Rate Relationship

The total work done is calculated as the product of the **efficiency** (rate) and the **time** taken: Work = Rate × Time.

Combined Efficiency

When multiple entities work simultaneously, their **individual rates** are additive: Rₜₒₜₐₗ = R₁ + R₂ + ... + Rₙ.

Time Conversion

To convert a fractional hour into minutes, **multiply the decimal portion** by 60. For example, 0.25 hours = 0.25 × 60 = 15 minutes.</p

questions.question: 8 men and 12 women can build a wall in 10 days. 6 men and 8 women can build the same wall in 14 days. How many more days will 1 woman take to build that wall alone compared to the number of days 1 man will take to build the wall?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Equating work efficiency: (8M + 12W) × 10 = (6M + 8W) × 14

⇒ 80M + 120W = 84M + 112W ⇒ 8W = 4M ⇒ **1M = 2W**

Efficiency ratio **M : W = 2 : 1**. Total Work = (8 × 2 + 12 × 1) × 10 = **280 units**.

Days for **1 Woman** = 280 ÷ 1 = 280 days; Days for **1 Man** = 280 ÷ 2 = 140 days.

Difference = 280 − 140 = **140 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 140 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: **8 men** and **12 women** build a wall in **10 days**.

Case 2: **6 men** and **8 women** build the wall in **14 days**.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = (M₁ × D₁) = (M₂ × D₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ (8M + 12W) × 10 = (6M + 8W) × 14

⇒ 80M + 120W = 84M + 112W

⇒ 120W − 112W = 84M − 80M

⇒ 8W = 4M ⇒ **1M = 2W**

⇒ Total Work (in terms of women) = (8 × 2W + 12W) × 10 = 28W × 10 = **280W units**

⇒ Time taken by **1 woman** alone = 280W ÷ 1W = **280 days**

⇒ Time taken by **1 man** alone = 280W ÷ 2W = **140 days**

Work Equivalence Formula

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a work. If 1M = 2W, then a man is twice as efficient as a woman and takes half the time.

Combined Rate Rule

Total efficiency of a group is the sum of the individual efficiencies of all members in that group.</p

questions.question: 48 men can do a work in 5 days while 40 women can do the same work in 9 days. In how many days can 4 men and 6 women together do the same work?

Using **M₁D₁ = M₂D₂**: 40 Women × 9 days = 12 Women × D₂.

⇒ D₂ = 360 ÷ 12 = 30 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 20 days and B can do the same work in 15 days. B worked alone for 6 days and left. In how many days can A complete the remaining work alone?
questions.solution:

Assume **Total Work** = LCM(20, 15) = 60 units.

Efficiency of **A** = 3 units/day and Efficiency of **B** = 4 units/day.

Work done by **B** in 6 days = 6 × 4 = 24 units.

**Remaining work** = 60 − 24 = 36 units.

Time taken by **A** = 36 ÷ 3 = 12 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **A** to complete work = 20 days

Time taken by **B** to complete work = 15 days

**B** worked alone for = 6 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

questions.question: Jitesh and Kamal can complete a certain piece of work in 7 and 16 days, respectively, They started to work together, and after 2 days, Kamal left. In how many days will Jitesh complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Jitesh can complete the work in 7 days

Kamal can complete the work in 16 days

They worked together for 2 days, then Kamal left

**Formula used:**

Work done by Jitesh in 1 day = 1/7

Work done by Kamal in 1 day = 1/16

Work done together in 1 day = (1/7) + (1/16)

Remaining work = Total work - Work done in 2 days

**Calculation:**

Work done together in 1 day = (1/7) + (1/16)

⇒ Work done together in 1 day = (16 + 7) / (7 × 16)

⇒ Work done together in 1 day = 23 / 112

Work done in 2 days = 2 × (23 / 112)

⇒ Work done in 2 days = 46 / 112

⇒ Work done in 2 days = 23 / 56

Remaining work = 1 - (23 / 56)

⇒ Remaining work = (56 - 23) / 56

⇒ Remaining work = 33 / 56

Jitesh's rate of work = 1 / 7

Time required by Jitesh to complete remaining work = Remaining work / Jitesh's rate of work

⇒ Time required by Jitesh = (33 / 56) / (1 / 7)

⇒ Time required by Jitesh = (33 / 56) × 7

⇒ Time required by Jitesh = 231 / 56

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

**Given:**

Time taken by Anjali (A) alone to do the work = 16 days.

Time taken by Anjali (A) and Ayushi (Y) together to do the work = 10 days.

Time taken by Anjali (A), Ayushi (Y), and Ankita (K) together to do the work = 8 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of the time taken by individuals/groups.

Efficiency = Total Work / Time Taken.

Combined Efficiency = Sum of the efficiencies of individuals working together.

Time taken together = Total Work / Combined Efficiency.

**Calculation:**

Let the total work be the LCM of 16, 10, and 8.

LCM(16, 10, 8) = LCM(2⁴, 2 × 5, 2³) = 2⁴ × 5 = 16 × 5 = 80 units.

Efficiency of Anjali (EA) = 80 / 16 = 5 units/day.

Efficiency of Anjali and Ayushi (EA ₊ Y) = 80 / 10 = 8 units/day.

Efficiency of Anjali, Ayushi, and Ankita (EA ₊ Y ₊ K) = 80 / 8 = 10 units/day.

The efficiency of Ayushi (EY):

EA₊Y = EA + EY

8 = 5 + EY

EY = 8 - 5 = 3 units/day.

The efficiency of Ankita (EK):

EA₊Y₊K = EA + EY + EK

10 = 5 + 3 + EK

10 = 8 + EK

EK = 10 - 8 = 2 units/day.

Combined efficiency of Anjali and Ankita (EA₊K):

EA₊K = EA + EK = 5 + 2 = 7 units/day.

Time taken by Anjali and Ankita together = 80 / 7 days.

**Anjali and Ankita can do the same work together in 80/7 days.**
